title: Agreement of 11 source-family fits did not prevent later climate forecast losses in German plant and crop phases
abstract: Can training diagnostics select safe climate forecasts for individual series in a new system? We learned linear decision rules from published model statistics for 20,942 series in 11 climate-response families. We tested them on 11,791 series in five later families. This is a retrospective transfer test; later family summaries were known before the methods were fixed. We scored decisions with a bounded MSE gain over a trailing mean. A context rule had equal-family mean gain 0.0228, compared with 0.0256 for a published false-signal gate and 0.0377 for its trend-preserving version. The context-minus-gate difference was -0.00285, with a whole-family bootstrap interval of -0.02274 to 0.01935. Requiring agreement from all 11 fits that omitted one source family reduced selections but did not prevent losses. Among selected late plant series, 55.1% lost more than 5% in MSE; among selected crop-phase series, 50.1% did. Cluster intervals were 51.6-58.5% and 47.7-52.7%. The same learned score scale was close to observed gain for spring plants and too high for late plants and crops. A ten-year trailing-level check kept the main ordering. The result limits the use of source-fit agreement as a safety check. It does not rule out other learned selectors. Only three later data sources were tested; observed weather and parent model limits apply.
